Shelves get album art, a scrollbar, any-edge resizing, rearranging and folder picking; the village stops overfilling; and Android gets a size slider.

**Shelves**
- **Album art and thumbnails on Linux**: real icons (and pixel art) now show a picture's own image, the cover art inside music files (MP3, FLAC, M4A, Ogg Vorbis / Opus), and an album folder's `cover.jpg`. Wide video thumbnails that downloaders embed are cropped to the square cover in the middle. (Windows already used the shell's thumbnails.)
- **A scrollbar**: a shelf with more than fits has one inside its right edge. Drag it, or click along it; the wheel works too. The bottom edge says which items are showing (*1–8 of 26*).
- **Resize from any edge or corner**: left, right, bottom and all four corners. The title row still moves the shelf, and a click on it rolls it up.
- **Rearrange**: drag an item to another spot on its own shelf. A gold marker shows where it'll go, and the order is kept.
- **Pick a folder**: *new shelf from a folder…* (right-click the bare scene) and *choose its folder…* (a shelf's menu) open the system's folder picker, so a shelf can show Music, Downloads or any other folder. The Shelves tab in settings has *folder…* and *+ from a folder…* too. A shelf still called "Shelf…" takes the folder's name.

**Visitors**
- **"Most at once" holds now**: passengers getting off the train didn't count towards it, so the village kept filling up however low it was set. They count now, and so do people coming back out of houses and igloos.

**The tray's settings window**
- The Effects tab shows each effect's live level bar, as the panel on the wallpaper does.
- Updates: it shows the running wallpaper's update status and has *check now* / *install*, which the wallpaper carries out.

**Android**
- **Size** (50% to 200%) replaces "detail" in the app's settings.
- The village keeps its size whichever way the screen is turned. A tablet or phone held sideways used to zoom right in; now it shows more of the village at the same size.
